# Herbal botanicals

N. Abdel-Rahman, Mohamed B. M. Ahmed, Bassem A. Sabry, Safaa S. M. Ali · 2019</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/abdel-rahman2019-egypt-nonalcoholic-beverages-metals">Heavy metals content in some non-alcoholic beverages (carbonated drinks, flavored yogurt drinks, and juice drinks) of the Egyptian markets</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Toxicology Reports</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/abdel-rahman2019-egypt-nonalcoholic-beverages-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/angelon-gaetz2018-lead-spices-north-carolina|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Angelon-Gaetz KA, Klaus C, Chaudhry EA, Bean DK · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/angelon-gaetz2018-lead-spices-north-carolina">Lead in Spices, Herbal Remedies, and Ceremonial Powders Sampled from Home Investigations for Children with Elevated Blood Lead Levels — North Carolina, 2011–2018</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">MMWR Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/angelon-gaetz2018-lead-spices-north-carolina">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/shchukin2022-mint-products-heavy-metals|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Shchukin VM, Blinkova EA, Kuzmina NE, Luttseva AI · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/shchukin2022-mint-products-heavy-metals">Evaluation of Elemental Impurities in Peppermint Herb and Peppermint-Based Herbal Products</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Regulatory Research and Medicine Evaluation</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/shchukin2022-mint-products-heavy-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</li>
<li>
<strong>Main drivers:</strong>

Herbal botanicals, as sold from grown independently had total mercury higher at 14.2 µg/kg, against 9.39 µg/kg for all samples in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/fischer2022-mercury-spice-plants-poland|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Fischer A, Brodziak-Dopierała B · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fischer2022-mercury-spice-plants-poland">The Mercury Concentration in Spice Plants</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Processes</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fischer2022-mercury-spice-plants-poland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</li>
<li>
<strong>Practical framing:</strong>

Ask for lot results with a quantification limit well below the limit that applies in the destination market.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/abdel-rahman2019-egypt-nonalcoholic-beverages-metals|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">G. N. Abdel-Rahman, Mohamed B. M. Ahmed, Bassem A. Sabry, Safaa S. M. Ali · 2019</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/abdel-rahman2019-egypt-nonalcoholic-beverages-metals">Heavy metals content in some non-alcoholic beverages (carbonated drinks, flavored yogurt drinks, and juice drinks) of the Egyptian markets</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Toxicology Reports</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/abdel-rahman2019-egypt-nonalcoholic-beverages-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/angelon-gaetz2018-lead-spices-north-carolina|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Angelon-Gaetz KA, Klaus C, Chaudhry EA, Bean DK · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/angelon-gaetz2018-lead-spices-north-carolina">Lead in Spices, Herbal Remedies, and Ceremonial Powders Sampled from Home Investigations for Children with Elevated Blood Lead Levels — North Carolina, 2011–2018</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">MMWR Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/angelon-gaetz2018-lead-spices-north-carolina">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/shchukin2022-mint-products-heavy-metals|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Shchukin VM, Blinkova EA, Kuzmina NE, Luttseva AI · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/shchukin2022-mint-products-heavy-metals">Evaluation of Elemental Impurities in Peppermint Herb and Peppermint-Based Herbal Products</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Regulatory Research and Medicine Evaluation</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/shchukin2022-mint-products-heavy-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Higher results came from contaminated or exposed settings rather than ordinary supply. Herbal botanicals, as sold from grown independently had total mercury higher at 14.2 µg/kg, against 9.39 µg/kg for all samples in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/fischer2022-mercury-spice-plants-poland|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Fischer A, Brodziak-Dopierała B · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fischer2022-mercury-spice-plants-poland">The Mercury Concentration in Spice Plants</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Processes</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fischer2022-mercury-spice-plants-poland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

For a buyer the practical points are the form bought, the basis a result is reported on, where the herbal botanicals came from and the laboratory’s reporting limit. Testing finds contamination but does not remove it.



<a id="ingredient-identity-and-scope"></a>
## What counts as herbal botanicals

<a id="hmi-ing-001"></a>
<a id="what-commodity-biological-species-edible-part-and-commercial-forms-does-this-page-cover"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-002"></a>
<a id="which-processing-states-and-derivatives-are-distinct-materials-rather-than-synonyms"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-003"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-can-be-transferred-between-those-materials-and-what-requires-a-separate-answer"></a>

This page covers herbal botanicals in 5 forms kept separate in every comparison: herbal botanicals, as sold (425 results), herbal botanicals, oil (49 results), herbal botanicals, powder or ground (15 results), herbal botanicals, dried (7 results) and herbal botanicals, flour or meal (6 results).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/abdel-rahman2019-egypt-nonalcoholic-beverages-metals|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">G. <div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-herbal-botanicals" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-herbal-botanicals-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of herbal botanicals, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

data-shared-occurrence-methods><summary>Shared dataset methods and interpretation</summary><div data-shared-evidence-content><p>Source summaries retain their original statistic, material, basis and censoring. Each source drawer identifies methods and overlapping samples. No matched reference or pooled distribution is inferred.</p></div></details><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-baseline-fallback id="hmi-reference-hmi-pooled-reference-v2:herbal-botanicals-bc1b5cfe5dcd:a46feaceae56"><summary>HMI herbal botanicals Pb reference · Herbal botanicals, as sold</summary><div data-baseline-reference-template="hmi-pooled-reference-v2:herbal-botanicals-bc1b5cfe5dcd:a46feaceae56"><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Reference and scope</p><p>HMI herbal botanicals Pb reference · Herbal botanicals, as sold. Herbal botanicals, as sold; As sold, as eaten or fresh weight, µg/kg; no moisture conversion. Distribution of subgroup median concentration values.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Reference (µg/kg)</th><th scope="col">Q1</th><th scope="col">Median</th><th scope="col">Q3</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Primary HMI reference</td><td>12.4–18.3 (bounded)</td><td>101–139 (bounded)</td><td>350–355 (bounded)</td></tr><tr><td>Alternative weighting</td><td>12.2–15.5 (bounded)</td><td>50–76 (bounded)</td><td>350–353 (bounded)</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p>78 reference units; 1 sampling family. Counts describe evidence units, not independent studies or certainty.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Contributing family</th><th scope="col">Reference units</th><th scope="col">Weight</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>WHO GEMS/Food</td><td>78</td><td>100%</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Methods</p><p>HMI pools subgroup medians for herbal botanicals, as sold on a as sold, as eaten or fresh weight basis: monitoring results summarized as one median per reporting region, sampling type and collection year, total diet composites and printed sample values as single observations, and printed subgroup medians from ordinary farms or markets. Each sampling family has equal total weight. Non-detects stay as zero-to-limit intervals, so quartiles carry lower and upper bounds. Means, ranges and maxima never enter as observations. Other forms, other bases, targeted sampling and results from mining, industrial, wastewater-affected, experimental, fertiliser or manufacturer settings are kept out of this reference.</p><p>Inverse weighted empirical CDF; midpoint at exact cumulative-weight boundaries. At least four reference units and a definitely positive Q1 to Q3 spread are required. This is a display eligibility rule, not statistical validation.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Limitations</p><p>WHO GEMS/Food is the only compatible sampling family for herbal botanicals, as sold on this basis in the completed herbal botanicals ledger, so this single-family reference cannot represent other markets. Reporting regions and purchase markets are not growing areas. Non-detects with differing limits widen the bounds. A position is descriptive concentration, not a safety or compliance judgment.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Admitted source families</p><ul><li><a href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants" class="internal" data-slug="sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants" data-no-cite-meta>WHO GEMS/Food</a></li></ul><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Reference version and interpretation</summary><p>Frozen evidence selection: 2026-10-22. <a id="sources-and-contamination-pathways"></a>
## How metals reach herbal botanicals

<a id="hmi-ing-010"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-supports-root-uptake-surface-deposition-feed-transfer-or-other-biological-pathways"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-011"></a>

<a id="which-source-attribution-claims-are-measured-modelled-inferred-or-unresolved"></a>

The evidence on how metals reach herbal botanicals comes from studies that compared exposed and ordinary settings. Herbal botanicals, as sold from grown independently had total mercury higher at 14.2 µg/kg, against 9.39 µg/kg for all samples in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/fischer2022-mercury-spice-plants-poland|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Fischer A, Brodziak-Dopierała B · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fischer2022-mercury-spice-plants-poland">The Mercury Concentration in Spice Plants</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Processes</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fischer2022-mercury-spice-plants-poland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

These are observational comparisons from single studies; the size of the difference depends on the site, metal and distance.

## Herbal botanicals FAQs

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-herbal-botanicals" data-anchor="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-herbal-botanicals" data-question="What heavy metals are found in herbal botanicals?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What heavy metals are found in herbal botanicals?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

The library reports lead, cadmium, total arsenic, inorganic arsenic, dimethylarsinic acid, total mercury, nickel, chromium, aluminium, tin, Co, Cu, Fe, Mn, Zn, V, Ba, Mo, Sr and Tl in herbal botanicals, most often lead, cadmium and total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/abdel-rahman2019-egypt-nonalcoholic-beverages-metals|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">G. N. Abdel-Rahman, Mohamed B. M. Ahmed, Bassem A. Sabry, Safaa S. M. Ali · 2019</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/abdel-rahman2019-egypt-nonalcoholic-beverages-metals">Heavy metals content in some non-alcoholic beverages (carbonated drinks, flavored yogurt drinks, and juice drinks) of the Egyptian markets</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Toxicology Reports</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/abdel-rahman2019-egypt-nonalcoholic-beverages-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/angelon-gaetz2018-lead-spices-north-carolina|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Angelon-Gaetz KA, Klaus C, Chaudhry EA, Bean DK · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/angelon-gaetz2018-lead-spices-north-carolina">Lead in Spices, Herbal Remedies, and Ceremonial Powders Sampled from Home Investigations for Children with Elevated Blood Lead Levels — North Carolina, 2011–2018</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">MMWR Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/angelon-gaetz2018-lead-spices-north-carolina">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/shchukin2022-mint-products-heavy-metals|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span href="../sources/shchukin2022-mint-products-heavy-metals">Evaluation of Elemental Impurities in Peppermint Herb and Peppermint-Based Herbal Products</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Regulatory Research and Medicine Evaluation</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/shchukin2022-mint-products-heavy-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> WHO GEMS/Food submissions reported lead in herbal botanicals, as sold from 1,791 results in 5 reporting regions, with subgroup medians from 2.2 to 1,690 µg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-herbal-botanicals" data-anchor="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-herbal-botanicals" data-question="How do heavy metals get into herbal botanicals?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How do heavy metals get into herbal botanicals?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In the studies available, herbal botanicals from contaminated or exposed settings carried more metal than herbal botanicals from the same study’s control.<sup class="cite">[[sources/fischer2022-mercury-spice-plants-poland|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Fischer A, Brodziak-Dopierała B · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fischer2022-mercury-spice-plants-poland">The Mercury Concentration in Spice Plants</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Processes</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fischer2022-mercury-spice-plants-poland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Herbal botanicals, as sold from grown independently had total mercury higher at 14.2 µg/kg, against 9.39 µg/kg for all samples in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/fischer2022-mercury-spice-plants-poland|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Fischer A, Brodziak-Dopierała B · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fischer2022-mercury-spice-plants-poland">The Mercury Concentration in Spice Plants</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Processes</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fischer2022-mercury-spice-plants-poland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-types-of-herbal-botanicals-have-the-lowest-levels" data-anchor="which-types-of-herbal-botanicals-have-the-lowest-levels" data-question="Which types of herbal botanicals have the lowest levels?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which types of herbal botanicals have the lowest levels?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

For lead, the HMI reference median was lowest for herbal botanicals, flour or meal (276 µg/kg) and highest for herbal botanicals, as sold (7,800 µg/kg); forms differ in water content, so this compares foods as sold or eaten, not uptake.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/assaad2020-lebanon-tabbouli-vegetables-metals|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Assaad N, Fadel D, Argyraki A, Kypritidou Z, Bakir A, Awad E · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/assaad2020-lebanon-tabbouli-vegetables-metals">Heavy Metals Accumulation in the Edible Vegetables of Lebanese Tabbouli Salad</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Agricultural Science 12(7):155-162</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/assaad2020-lebanon-tabbouli-vegetables-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/mehari2015-north-carolina-fruits-vegetables-processed-foods|12]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Mehari TF, Greene L, Duncan AL, Fakayode SO · 2015</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/mehari2015-north-carolina-fruits-vegetables-processed-foods">Trace and Macro Elements Concentrations in Selected Fresh Fruits, Vegetables, Herbs, and Processed Foods in North Carolina, USA</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Environmental Protection, 2015, 6, 573-583</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/mehari2015-north-carolina-fruits-vegetables-processed-foods">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/sultana2021-dhaka-stem-vegetables-metals|13]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Sultana R, Chamon AS, Mondol MN · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/sultana2021-dhaka-stem-vegetables-metals">Heavy metal concentration in commonly sold stem vegetables in Dhaka city market and probable health risk</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Dhaka University Journal of Biological Sciences 2021, 30(2): 221-232</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/sultana2021-dhaka-stem-vegetables-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-herbal-botanicals" data-anchor="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-herbal-botanicals" data-question="Which regions report the lowest levels in herbal botanicals?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which regions report the lowest levels in herbal botanicals?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Among GEMS/Food reporting regions, herbal botanicals, as sold had the lowest lead subgroup median in PAHO (2.2 µg/kg) and the highest in SEARO (1,690 µg/kg); reporting regions are markets, not growing areas.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> For cadmium, the lowest regional median was in PAHO (13.5 µg/kg) and the highest in PAHO (250 µg/kg).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="does-processing-change-heavy-metals-in-herbal-botanicals" data-anchor="does-processing-change-heavy-metals-in-herbal-botanicals" data-question="Does processing change heavy metals in herbal botanicals?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Does processing change heavy metals in herbal botanicals?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Only comparisons between forms in the same study are available, not before-and-after measurements of the same herbal botanicals.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Herbal botanicals, flour or meal (EURO) had lead lower at 233 µg/kg, against 338 µg/kg for the unprocessed form in the same group (herbal botanicals, as sold).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-herbal-botanicals-is-inorganic" data-anchor="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-herbal-botanicals-is-inorganic" data-question="How much of the arsenic in herbal botanicals is inorganic?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How much of the arsenic in herbal botanicals is inorganic?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Inorganic arsenic, the more toxic form, was measured in 7 results from 2 sources, far fewer than total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs|15]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) · 2014</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs">Dietary exposure to inorganic arsenic in the European population</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">EFSA Journal 2014;12(3):3597</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) 2014 reported inorganic arsenic at 260 µg/kg (mean) in herbal botanicals, as sold from European dietary-survey occurrence data.<sup class="cite">[[sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs|15]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) · 2014</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs">Dietary exposure to inorganic arsenic in the European population</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">EFSA Journal 2014;12(3):3597</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>
